findings.title: Destruction executor decides eligibility from a legal-hold boolean computed BEFORE its claim; a hold placed mid-execution does not stop byte deletion + certificate

evidence.snippet: const claim = await prisma.evidence.updateMany({ where: { id: input.evidenceId, OR: [ { lifecycleState: "TRASHED" }, ...
const res = await storage.deleteObjectVersion({ ...target, versionId: v.versionId });
await tx.evidence.update({ where: { id: evidence.id }, data: { lifecycleState: "DESTROYED", destroyedAtUtc: now,
const hold = (await client.evidenceLegalHold.create({ data: { teamId: input.teamId, scope, evidenceId, caseId,

findings.observed: The hold verdict is read by the caller (orchestrator :169, also processor.ts:5668/5688, destruction-review.service.ts:658/670, destruction-governance.service.ts:579/590) and passed as a boolean. The executor re-reads the evidence row after its claim but never re-reads evidence_legal_holds. placeCanonicalLegalHold only verifies the tenant (:264-286) and inserts; it neither checks lifecycleState PENDING_DESTRUCTION nor takes any lock shared with the executor. The S3 object-lock legal-hold backstop (executor :446-462) only reacts to object-level holds, which application holds do not set.
findings.expected: A hold committed before bytes are deleted must block destruction (re-evaluate effective hold inside/after the claim, or serialize hold placement against PENDING_DESTRUCTION).
findings.dataFlow: orchestrator reads holds -> executeEvidenceDestruction(legalHold=false) -> claim -> computeEvidenceDestructionEligibility(input.legalHold) -> S3 list/delete all versions -> tombstone + EVIDENCE_PURGED + certificate
findings.rootCause: TOCTOU: hold is an input parameter rather than re-read under the claim.
findings.blastRadius: Every destruction entry point (4 callers) for WORKSPACE evidence.
findings.impact: Original evidence under an active legal hold is irreversibly destroyed and a destruction certificate is issued.
findings.reproduction: 1) Evidence E trashed with grace expired. 2) Pause orchestrator after gatherDestructionFacts. 3) Place EVIDENCE hold on E (succeeds 200). 4) Resume: executor deletes all versions and tombstones E.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration test with real PG: stub storage to block on first deleteObjectVersion; place hold via placeCanonicalLegalHold in parallel; assert executor outcome is DESTROYED (defect) vs BLOCKED.
findings.remediation: Inside the executor, after the claim and immediately before the first delete, call evaluateEffectiveLegalHold(tx) and release the claim if held; make placeCanonicalLegalHold refuse (or flag) when lifecycleState='PENDING_DESTRUCTION' with a live claim, under the same pg_advisory_xact_lock(evidenceId).
findings.acceptanceProof: Concurrency test above returns BLOCKED/LEGAL_HOLD_ACTIVE and bytes remain.

findings.title: Restore-from-trash 'succeeds' (200 + EVIDENCE_RESTORED custody) while the destruction executor holds its claim; executor then tombstones the restored record

findings.observed: PENDING_DESTRUCTION is not a product state, so resolveEvidenceProductState falls back to deletedAt -> TRASHED and restore is allowed; both restore and tombstone write by id only with no state predicate and no shared lock.
findings.expected: Restore must fail (409) while a destruction claim is live, or the tombstone must be conditional on lifecycleState='PENDING_DESTRUCTION' with the claim timestamp.
findings.dataFlow: Worker executor claim (evidence.lifecycleState=PENDING_DESTRUCTION, deletedAt still set) -> user POST /v1/evidence/:id/restore -> applyEvidenceLifecycleAction -> resolveEvidenceProductState falls back to trashedAt => TRASHED -> canRestoreFromTrash -> tx.evidence.update by id (ACTIVE) + EVIDENCE_RESTORED custody -> executor deletes S3 versions -> tx.evidence.update by id (DESTROYED).
findings.rootCause: PENDING_DESTRUCTION is not a product state, so the capability model sees a trashed record; both the restore write and the tombstone write are unconditional by id with no shared lock.
findings.blastRadius: Any trashed workspace or personal evidence whose grace has expired and is being destroyed by any of the 4 executor callers; affects the restoring user and the custody ledger.
findings.impact: User told evidence is restored (custody says restored) but it is destroyed with a certificate: false success + evidence loss.
findings.reproduction: Block executor after claim; POST /restore -> 200; resume; row DESTROYED.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration test with blocking storage stub as in SEC-01.
findings.remediation: Restore/lifecycle writes use updateMany with lifecycleState predicate excluding PENDING_DESTRUCTION + count check; tombstone updateMany where {id, lifecycleState:'PENDING_DESTRUCTION', destructionClaimedAtUtc: now}.
findings.acceptanceProof: Concurrent test returns 409 for restore or executor aborts.

findings.title: Existence oracles: 404-vs-403 on case access, capture sessions, cases evidence attach, evidence create with foreign teamId; public verify 409 exposes status of unfinalized records
findings.observed: UUIDv4 ids make blind enumeration infeasible; ids leak via verify URLs.
findings.expected: Uniform 404.
findings.dataFlow: GET /v1/evidence?caseId= -> assertCaseAccess (404 missing / 403 foreign); GET /v1/capture/sessions/:id -> loadOwnedDraft (404/403); POST /v1/evidence with foreign teamId -> 403; GET /public/verify/:id unfinalized -> 409 with status.
findings.rootCause: These handlers predate the anti-enumeration convention and return distinct status codes for existing-but-forbidden objects.
findings.blastRadius: Any authenticated user holding a UUID (or anyone with a verify id); existence/status disclosure only.
findings.impact: Low.
findings.reproduction: As an outsider GET /v1/evidence?caseId=<existing foreign case> -> 403 vs <random uuid> -> 404; GET /public/verify/<uploading evidence id> -> 409 with status.
findings.remediation: Return 404 uniformly.
findings.acceptanceProof: Route tests.

findings.title: Annotation PATCH accepts any evidencePartId (no ownership check, unlike POST)

findings.rootCause: The PATCH schema is AnnotationBody.partial() and the ownership check exists only in the POST handler.
findings.blastRadius: Annotations in any workspace; integrity of annotation-part references only.

findings.remediation: Validate part ownership.
findings.acceptanceProof: PATCH with foreign part -> 400.
